purpose: Entry-level and convention-level metadata comparison separating the contribution of Hubbard-U from magnetic-initialization differences between Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT, using each project's documented, installed-package source code rather than new calculations.

materials_project_workflow.source_inspected: pymatgen (installed) io/vasp/VASPIncarBase.yaml and io/vasp/sets.py (DictSet._get_incar MAGMOM/LDAUU assembly logic), which MPRelaxSet (the input-set class derived from the Materials Project production workflow) inherits from

U_values_confirmed.gated_on: O or F anion present, same list as used in hubbard_u_feature.py

materials_project_workflow.finding: All default per-element initial MAGMOM values in pymatgen's VASPIncarBase.yaml (which MPRelaxSet uses) are positive, i.e. a uniform-sign, high-spin-per-element starting guess rather than an alternating/antiferromagnetic pattern, unless the input Structure already carries per-site magmom/spin (e.g. from an external magnetic-ordering enumeration upstream of pymatgen's input-set code; this inspection cannot confirm whether that is applied to every MP entry, since the MP production infrastructure, atomate, is a separate, larger codebase that was not fully inspected). The most directly confirmed computational-choice difference between the two databases is therefore the U value itself; the initial magnetic configuration may be similarly uniform-sign in both workflows for many entries.

jarvis_dft_workflow.source_inspected: jarvis-tools (installed) tasks/vasp/vasp.py (JobFactory class: __init__ optional_params default dict, workflow()/steps list, magorder() method) and io/vasp/inputs.py (find_ldau_magmom, add_ldau_incar)
jarvis_dft_workflow.ldau_default_confirmed: optional_params = {..., 'ldau': False, 'Uval': 2.0, ...} (JobFactory.__init__ default). The standard bulk high-throughput entry point used to build the dft_3d table, all_optb88vdw_calcs() -> workflow(), does not override this, so no +U correction is applied in the JARVIS standard OptB88vdW workflow.
jarvis_dft_workflow.magnetic_ordering_search_confirmed: workflow()'s steps list includes a 'MAGORDER' step; JobFactory.magorder() calls MagneticOrdering(atoms=self.atoms).get_minimum_configs(min_configs=3), which enumerates at least 3 symmetry-distinct magnetic configurations (FM/AFM/FiM-type site-resolved spin patterns, not a single uniform guess) and runs a separate VASP job for each. This magnetic-ordering search step is not gated by the ldau flag: it runs whether or not +U is applied.
jarvis_dft_workflow.initialization_framing: The description of JARVIS-DFT as computing magnetic-moment entries from spin-polarized calculations initialized only from a ferromagnetic starting configuration is an oversimplification: the documented workflow searches multiple magnetic orderings, including AFM-type configurations, via the MAGORDER step when that step is executed. Whether the released dft_3d table's magmom_oszicar field reflects the lowest-energy configuration selected by the MAGORDER step or an earlier single-configuration RELAX step could not be resolved from source-code inspection alone and remains an open point.
jarvis_dft_workflow.corroborating_public_documentation: JARVIS-DB's own DFT documentation page (jarvis-materials-design.github.io/dbdocs/jarvisdft/) states that geometry optimization uses spin-polarized calculations with an initial magnetic moment of 1 uB/atom by default -- consistent with a uniform per-atom starting guess at the RELAX stage specifically, separate from the later MAGORDER exploration.

causal_summary: The most direct, isolated and confirmed computational-choice difference between the two databases, verifiable from each project's installed source code, is the application of the Hubbard-U correction itself: Materials Project applies documented, species-dependent U values (Co/Cr/Fe/Mn/Mo/Ni/V/W) via its MPRelaxSet-derived workflow, whereas the JARVIS-DFT standard bulk OptB88vdW workflow has ldau=False as a default and does not apply U. The magnetic-initialization explanation is less clear-cut: JARVIS does search multiple magnetic orderings (not only a single ferromagnetic guess), but without +U, so even a correctly identified AFM-type spin pattern computed under plain GGA lacks the orbital-dependent potential needed to localize correlated d-electrons and stabilize an insulating or semiconducting AFM ground state (standard correlated-electron DFT physics; Anisimov, Dudarev, Cococcioni). The absence of +U, rather than only the absence of an AFM-ordering search, is therefore the more defensible explanation for the spuriously large reported moments of JARVIS on antiferromagnetic transition-metal oxides.
